Subject: Processing locations and cross-border handling — quick Qs

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. A few compliance folks at Cygnus asked for a short Q&A so we can move this to procurement. Can you confirm the following at a high level?

- Where is customer request data (API input/payloads) processed and stored for Redwood's hosted API (regions/locations)?
- Do you use subprocessors outside the EEA (India, Brazil, US) for any part of request processing or support?
- How does cross-border routing happen in an outage (failover to other regions)?
- Default retention windows for logs, prompts, embeddings; and deletion guarantees when a customer requests deletion
- Is BYOK / customer-managed keys available for hosted?

If you already have a one-page map or inventory we could pass to our legal team, that would help. Ideally we get this back by end of week — procurement is on a tight timeline.

Thanks,
Emma Jones
CTO Office
Cygnus Fintech
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Processing locations and cross-border handling — quick Qs

Emma — great to hear from you, glad the demo was useful. High-level answers below; attaching a regional map and our subprocessor inventory for immediate review (see attachments). Rafael and Laura are copied for procurement/contract and SOC2 follow-up.

1) Processing locations (hosted API):
   - Primary processing occurs in the region selected by the customer: EU (eu-west-1), US (us-west-2 / us-east-1).
   - Model inference & KV/prefix caching are colocated in the same region for hosted customers. Temporary caches are not replicated cross-region by default.

2) Subprocessors outside EEA:
   - Core cloud providers: AWS (US/EU), GCP (US), Azure (EU/US) depending on deployment.
   - CDN/edge: Fastly/Cloudflare (global).
   - Observability: DataDog (US/EU).
   - No routine use of India-based subprocessors for core inference; some optional third-party integrators (support vendors) may be located in APAC but that can be excluded in enterprise contracts.

3) Cross-border routing & failover:
   - For hosted API, we prefer regional affinity. In the event of regional outage we fail over to a compatible fallback region to maintain availability (this may result in cross-border processing).
   - For customers with strict residency requirements we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private (VPC) where you can pin workloads to a region and we disable automatic cross-region failover.

4) Retention & deletion:
   - Default: request/usage logs retained 30 days; embeddings/derived artifacts retained 90 days by default (used for caching/quality).
   - Customers can request immediate deletion of their data; for hosted customers deletion is executed within our deletion pipeline and confirmed within 72 hours for primary data, with longer tails for backups (we document backup deletion windows in the DPA).

5) Encryption & keys:
   - All data at-rest is encrypted using cloud provider KMS.
   - BYOK (customer-managed keys) is available for Redwood Dedicated and Private. For hosted customers we offer a managed KMS option and can discuss customer-specific key management in enterprise contracts.

Next steps: attached a one-page regional map and the subprocessor inventory CSV. Rafael — can you attach SOC2 and DPA template to this thread? Laura — any redlines we should flag early for Emma?

Best,
Kimberly Park

Gareth — good questions. I'll answer point-by-point below. I've also attached the SCC addendum we reference in our DPA for your legal team.

- EU-only processing: For hosted customers selecting an EU region, normal inference and caching remain within EU data centers. However, automatic failover for availability may cross-border to a fallback region unless you sign a residency SLA (available as part of Dedicated/Private or as an add-on). We can contractually prohibit cross-region failover for EU personal data in the DPA if that is a strict requirement.

- Subprocessors in India/Brazil: We do not use India or Brazil-based subprocessors for core inference. Some optional vendor services (e.g., commercial support partners, third-party UX testing) may operate in APAC/Latin America. Those are explicitly listed in the subprocessor inventory CSV and can be excluded by enterprise agreement.

- Embeddings retention & per-workspace auto-delete: Default retention for embeddings is 90 days; we offer per-workspace lifecycle policies for Dedicated/Private customers. For hosted customers we can expose an API flag for auto-delete and shorten retention on request (subject to operational limits).

Operational notes: backups are retained per our backup retention schedule; we include backup deletion timelines in the DPA. Transfers from EU to US rely on SCCs and our transfer addendum; we are prepared to execute additional contractual assurances if Cygnus requires them.

Let me know if you'd like us to mark specific subprocessors "excluded for Cygnus" in the inventory prior to contract execution — Rafael can take that action.

Cheers,
Kimberly
